question_text: A 3:2:1 profit-sharing ratio is used for three government project partners. If total profit is P360,000, what is the difference between the largest and smallest share?

hint_ladder.title: Think in Parts
hint_ladder.text: The ratio 3:2:1 means the profit is divided into equal chunks. Add 3+2+1=6 total chunks. Each chunk gets an equal share of P360,000.

hint_ladder.title: Find the Value of One Chunk
hint_ladder.text: Divide P360,000 by 6 = P60,000 per chunk. Each partner's share is simply their number of chunks × P60,000.

hint_ladder.title: Identify the Extreme Shares
hint_ladder.text: Largest share = 3 chunks × P60,000 = P180,000. Smallest share = 1 chunk × P60,000 = P60,000.

hint_ladder.title: Almost There
hint_ladder.text: Subtract smallest from largest: P180,000 – P60,000 = P120,000. Shortcut: 3–1=2 chunks difference, so 2 × P60,000 = P120,000.

B.text: You might have chosen B because you miscalculated the total parts or the value per part—double-check that the ratios sum to 6, not 5 or a...

C.text: Correct. With 6 total parts at P60,000 each, the difference is (3–1)×P60,000 = P120,000.

D.text: You might have chosen D because you overestimated by using the wrong operation order—first get the correct per-part value from the total,...

next_time_rule: For difference between largest and smallest ratio shares, sum the ratios, then multiply (largest–smallest) by the value per part.
deconstruct_text:
Okay, let’s break it down, kapatid. The 3:2:1 ratio means the profit from the barangay project is divided into equal parts. Each partner gets shares in these proportions. First, we sum the ratio numbers: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 total parts.

The total profit is P360,000. So each part’s value = P360,000 ÷ 6 = P60,000. Largest share: 3 parts × P60,000 = P180,000. Smallest share: 1 part × P60,000 = P60,000.

Difference = P180,000 – P60,000 = P120,000. Mental shortcut: difference in ratio is 3–1=2 parts. 2 × P60,000 = P120,000 agad. Laging double-check kung hanggang saan ang comparison para iwas sa trap.
